task.title: Build customization-control plugin
task.objective: Develop a high-quality, reliable cross-provider customization-control plugin that audits, deduplicates, repairs, syncs, and publishes agent customizations across Codex, Claude Code, and Kimi Code without degrading into a CLI-only wrapper.

constraints: Target all three providers: Codex, Claude Code, Kimi Code.
Use official provider documentation before asserting customization syntax, install paths, plugin manifests, marketplace fields, MCP config shapes, or skill discovery behavior.
Skills must contain decision logic, trigger surface, safety policy, and recovery workflow; scripts are deterministic helpers only.
Highest reliability standard: inventory before mutation, dry-run plan before repair, explicit safety classes, backups/quarantine for risky removals, validation after every applied change.
Windows-first implementation. PowerShell-safe path handling and resolved absolute path checks.
Marketplace support is in scope only for already-ported plugins.
decisions: Six skills: customization-audit (entrypoint), customization-dedupe, customization-sync, customization-repair, marketplace-manager, windows-customization-guard (internal).
Dedupe categories: canonical, provider-link, duplicate-copy, stale-cache, conflict, broken-link, unknown.
Safe default flow: inventory -> plan -> apply deterministic safe repairs -> quarantine risky removals -> revalidate -> report.
Scripts live under scripts/ with dry-run and structured JSON output.
References encode policies: known roots, dedupe policy, repair policy, marketplace policy.
Plugin distributed via 0langas-plugin-marketplace as git submodule.
open_questions: User wants to move away from ~/.agents/skills as a root — prefers provider-specific roots (.codex, .claude, .kimi-code). customization-dedupe/sync could help migrate.
Confirm whether initial implementation should handle macOS/Linux roots or stay Windows-only in references.

done: Scaffolded full plugin structure: .claude-plugin/, .codex-plugin/, skills/, scripts/, references/, tests/.
Implemented all 6 skills with SKILL.md frontmatter, decision logic, safety policies, and recovery workflows.
Implemented 4 reference policy files: known-roots.json, dedupe-policy.json, repair-policy.json, marketplace-policy.json.
Implemented 5 PowerShell helper scripts: inventory.ps1, validate.ps1, plan-dedupe.ps1, apply-dedupe.ps1, quarantine.ps1. All support -OutputFormat json|table and -DryRun.
Wrote 24 Pester tests — all pass on Pester 5.8.0.
Created cross-provider manifests for Codex (.codex-plugin/plugin.json with interface block) and Kimi Code (kimi.plugin.json with sessionStart/skillInstructions).
Added as git submodule to 0langas-plugin-marketplace. Updated all 4 marketplace JSON files.
Installed in Codex: codex plugin add customization-control@0langas-plugins — shows installed+enabled.
Verified Claude Code: claude plugin validate passes, all 6 skills discovered.
Verified Codex: codex exec audit returns 118 items, 10 broken links, 16 duplicate groups.
Verified Kimi Code: kimi -p audit returns identical results (118/10/16).
Fixed Join-Path 3-arg compat issue for PowerShell 5.1.
current: Plugin is functional and tested across all 3 providers.
Ready for next iteration: implementing actual dedupe/repair/sync execution workflows.
next: Implement actual deduplication workflow: run plan-dedupe, present dry-run to user, execute apply-dedupe with quarantine.
Implement sync workflow: detect missing provider links, create junctions/symlinks.
Implement repair workflow: fix 10 broken symlinks in ~/.claude/skills/ (junctions pointing to deleted ~/.agents/skills/ targets).
Consider migrating user's skills from ~/.agents/skills/ to provider-specific roots per user preference.
Add integration tests for full audit->plan->apply pipeline.

privacy_notes: No secrets captured. Local paths included for task context.
